label: b44: continue the 4 best b29/b40 checkpoints to 3M, lr 1e-7
notes:
Continues b29b-chase10g75seed2 from its own best checkpoint, ckpt-1447000 (99.0% over 500 episodes, rank 1 of 8 and the project record), to an absolute 3M-step cap with SNEK_LEARNING_RATE=1e-7 the only change from b42. Seed matches the source arm.

Third rung of the learning-rate ladder on the same four seeded champions: b42 = 1e-5 (the rate these checkpoints were trained at), b43 = 1e-6 on the laptop, b44 = 1e-7 here. Seeds, config and source checkpoints are identical across all three, so the three batches are a paired dose-response on one knob. Config is b29's: fc320, chase-safe c=0.10 gate 75, IS off, target_update 1000, discount 0.9975, food-distance 0, fork_branches 4, and NO free-space shaping.

WHY THIS RUNG. b42 answered the original question and answered it negatively: over the first 352k steps past resume (the largest window matched across all eight arms), the four 1e-5 arms lost about 5 pp of banded mean self-eval perfect rate and settled at a lower plateau: 93.6 -> 91.6 -> 89.1 -> 89.5 across 0-100k / 100-200k / 200-300k / 300-385k. The four 1e-6 arms stayed flat over the same bands -- 95.4 -> 96.3 -> 96.2 -> 95.6 -- and led on 4 of 4 seeds in every band after the first (+4.7, +7.1, +6.1 pp). best_perfect30 agrees on all four seeds: 93.3-97.7 at 1e-5 against 98.3-100.0 at 1e-6, and strong_eval_fraction 87.0-97.9 against 97.9-99.8. So lowering the rate 10x converted a one-time decay into a hold, and on one seed into a gain -- b43b reached a 100.0 best-30 window 320k steps past its own seed checkpoint. b44 asks where lowering the rate stops helping.

DO NOT USE peak_trailing TO JUDGE THESE ARMS. It is trailing average SCORE, which maxes at 95/95, and all eight arms read exactly 95.0 with the peak timestamped at their seed step -- the metric is saturated from the first eval because these policies already play a full board. Read perfect_percent, best_perfect30 or strong_eval_fraction instead. An earlier pass here misread that saturation as 'no arm ever beat its starting checkpoint', which was wrong.

PRE-REGISTERED READINGS, written before launch.
(1) NULL vs b43 -- the expected outcome, ~65%. If 1e-6 is already doing nothing but failing to damage the policy, 1e-7 cannot do better than the same nothing, and the two batches land inside each other's noise. That is a real result: it bounds the useful range and says the preservation effect saturates by 1e-6.
(2) b44 WORSE than b43 -- ~10%, and the most informative outcome. It would mean b43 is not merely holding but actively repairing something -- most plausibly adapting to the transplanted replay buffer, which comes from the source arm's final step and is therefore slightly off-policy for the restored weights -- and that 1e-6 is roughly the rate at which repair keeps pace with drift. 1e-7 would then be too slow to repair while still being perturbed by continued exploration.
(3) b44 BETTER than b43 -- ~25%. Decay at 1e-6 is still nonzero and the optimum is below it; the ladder should be extended to 1e-8.
Note the asymmetry: the user's stated interest is 'when does this start failing', and the most likely failure mode at a low rate is STASIS, not collapse. Do not read 'no improvement' as a broken arm -- read it against b43's curve, which is the control for exactly that.

TRIPWIRE. Adam's learning_rate is a checkpointed tf.Variable, so initialize_or_restore() puts the saved 1e-5 back and SNEK_LEARNING_RATE was a silent no-op on every resume in this project before training.enforce_learning_rate (2026-08-18, deployed here at 5f1593c97). Each arm MUST print
  learning rate: checkpoint restored 1e-05, reset to the configured 1e-07
at startup. If that line is absent the arm is training at 1e-5, it is a second copy of b42, and the batch measures nothing -- check it before reading any result.

SEEDING. The policy dir was pre-seeded by hyperparamTuning/scripts/seed_from_checkpoint.sh rather than resumed in place: it holds arch.json, one ckpt pair, a copy of the source arm's replay_buffer, and a 'checkpoint' state file naming only that step. initialize_or_restore() would otherwise take the source's LAST step rather than its best; resuming in place would overwrite the very arm the selection was made from; and a dir with exactly one pre-existing checkpoint guarantees every later ckpt-* belongs to this run, so the close-out cannot mix two arms' weights at the same step. The buffer is carried deliberately -- without it a 5k-step test of a 98% policy fell 80% -> 50% perfect, and held 90-100% with it.
